research.job_description_summary: Amazon hires new graduates in India as Software Development Engineers (SDE I). A 2026 candidate account describes an online assessment with two medium-to-hard DSA questions, then onsite and virtual rounds: two DSA rounds (one with project discussion and Leadership Principles questions), a hiring manager round with a generative-AI segment, one DSA problem and one system design, and a bar raiser round that is behavioral only. The official Amazon careers pages were not fetched.
required_skills: Use and verification of generative AI tools
limitations: Amazon's official careers pages were not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.
All class B items trace to one LeetCode Discuss account (April 2026, interviews on 6 and 14 April); a second account (1Point3Acres, February 2026 OA) is behind a login wall and could not be read.
The online assessment problems are not named in the account; all ten OA items are original practice problems matching the reported format, not reported questions.

Reported problems (rotated-array search, circular maximum subarray, number of islands, a subarray problem with a difference condition between endpoints, lowest common ancestor) are rewritten originally; the LCA item uses a parent-array tree for a testable input format, which generalises the binary-tree wording.
Leadership Principles questions beyond the two named bar raiser themes are original prompts covering the principles.
Interview details can vary by team and year; the single account may not represent the general process.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.
